QF.id: Role of RTAs in Mutual Fund Transactions_39

question.text: The ETCD (Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives) schemes must publish their NAV by what time?

answer.text: 3 PM on the same business day (T-day)
9 AM on the next business day (T+1)
11 PM on the same business day (T-day)
10 AM on the next business day (T+1)

explanation.text: The Logic: NAV publication timelines for different mutual fund scheme categories are framed around when the underlying securities can be reliably priced. Standard open-ended (non-FoF) schemes invested in domestic listed securities can be valued the same business day and have a same-day (11 PM) deadline. Fund-of-Fund and overseas schemes depend on the NAVs/closing prices of underlying funds and foreign markets, so they get a next-business-day deadline (10 AM T+1). Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives (ETCD) schemes depend on commodity exchange settlement prices, which often become available only after late commodity-market hours, so ETCD schemes are given a T+1 deadline (9 AM T+1 per industry practice) - later than the same-day rule but aligned with the next-morning availability of settlement prices. The Trap: 11 PM same-day is the deadline for non-FoF, non-ETCD schemes - it does not apply to ETCDs whose settlement prices come in later. 10 AM T+1 is the deadline for FoF/overseas schemes, not ETCD schemes. 3 PM same-day has no regulatory basis as a NAV publication deadline. Note: The cited workbook pages (94, 101, 130, 136, 138 of the NISM Series II-B Registrars and Transfer Agents - Mutual Fund workbook) describe the 11 PM same-day rule for non-FoF schemes, the 10 AM T+1 rule for FoF schemes, and note that ETCDs are excluded from the stipulated-time statement - but they do not explicitly state the 9 AM T+1 ETCD deadline. The framing above reflects industry/SEBI-circular practice for ETCD NAV publication and should be cross-checked against the latest SEBI circular before being relied upon operationally.
